response_text: These two mechanisms—yielding and time-based pre-emptive context switching—can work together because they complement each other in controlling thread execution. Yielding allows a thread to voluntarily give up the CPU early when it knows it can wait or wants to let others run, improving efficiency by avoiding unnecessary timer interrupts. Meanwhile, the time-based pre-emptive mechanism ensures that no thread can monopolize the CPU indefinitely by forcibly interrupting it after its time slice expires, guaranteeing fairness and responsiveness. The OS scheduler handles both cases by performing context switches either when a thread calls osYield or when the timer interrupt signals that the current thread’s time slice is over. This hybrid approach combines the predictability and efficiency of cooperative yielding with the robustness of pre-emptive multitasking, ensuring smooth and fair thread management.\n
